contests.title: Siloam Springs — Wastewater Bonds and Tax

provenance.quote:
Bonds of the City of Siloam Springs in
the maximum aggregate principal
amount of $55,000,000 for the purpose
of financing all or a portion of the costs
of extensions, betterments and
improvements to the City's wastewater
facilities, including particularly, without
limitation, wastewater treatment plant
and sewer collection infrastructure,
and, in order to pay the bonds, the levy
and pledge of a 0.625% local sales
and use tax within the City.
If the bonds are approved, there will be
levied within the City a 0.625% local
sales and use tax (the "Bond Tax"), the
net collections of which remaining after
deduction of the administrative charges
of the State of Arkansas and required
rebates will be used solely to retire or
pay obligations with respect to the
bonds in accordance with Amendment
No. 62 to the Arkansas Constitution.
The Bond Tax will expire after the
bonds have been paid or provision is
made therefor in accordance with
Arkansas statutes. The Bond Tax will
replace the City's existing 0.625%
sales and use tax levied in 2018 for the
purpose of retiring bonds to finance
water improvements (the "2018 Tax").
The effective date of the Bond Tax will
be the day following the date that the
2018 Tax expires. Proceeds of the
bonds may fund a debt service reserve
and pay expenses of issuing the
bonds. The bonds may be issued at
one time or in series from time to time.

measures.questionText:
The bonds described below that are
approved may be combined into a single
issue or may be issued in series from time
to time. If the bonds for one or more of the
purposes are approved and one of such
purposes is the Refunding Bonds, there
will be levied a new 1% sales and use tax,
the net collections of which remaining after
deduction of the administrative charges of
the State of Arkansas and required rebates
will be used solely to retire the bonds and
obligations of the City with respect thereto.
The tax will replace the City's existing 1%
sales and use tax levied in 2018 for the
sole purpose of retiring bonds. The
effective date of the new tax will be the day
following the date the existing tax expires.
The rate of taxation will be 1% even if
bonds for more than one purpose are
approved. No bonds will be issued for any
purpose unless the Refunding Bonds are
also approved. The 1% sales and use tax
will expire after the bonds have been paid
or provision is made therefor in
accordance with Arkansas statutes.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds a 1% city sales and use tax in Little Flock to pay for general city operations.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional 1% sales and use tax for city operations.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject the additional 1% city sales and use tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Lets Rogers borrow up to $118 million to refinance its 2018B and 2022 sales-tax bonds. A replacement 1% sales and use tax would repay the bonds, beginning the day after the existing bond tax expires and ending when repayment is completed or otherwise legally provided for. The rate stays at 1% even if several bond questions pass, and no bonds in the package can be issued unless this refunding question passes.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the refinancing bonds and replacement 1% sales and use tax, allowing other approved bonds in the package to proceed.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject these refinancing bonds; no other bonds in this package could then be issued.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Lets Rogers borrow up to $195.5 million for streets, roads, trails and bridges, with related drainage, flood-control, lighting, sidewalks, traffic signals and utility work. The bonds depend on approval of the separate refunding-bonds question. A replacement 1% city sales and use tax would repay approved bonds; it replaces the existing bond tax beginning the day after that tax expires, stays at 1% even if several bond questions pass, and ends when the bonds are paid or payment is otherwise legally provided for.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize up to $195.5 million in bonds for these improvements, subject to approval of the refunding question and repayment through the replacement 1% tax.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this bond authorization for this purpose; the other bond questions are decided separately.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Lets Rogers borrow up to $81.5 million for parks and recreation facilities, including related land, parking, equipment, drainage, roads, trails and utility work. The bonds depend on approval of the separate refunding-bonds question. A replacement 1% city sales and use tax would repay approved bonds; it replaces the existing bond tax beginning the day after that tax expires, stays at 1% even if several bond questions pass, and ends when the bonds are paid or payment is otherwise legally provided for.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize up to $81.5 million in bonds for these improvements, subject to approval of the refunding question and repayment through the replacement 1% tax.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this bond authorization for this purpose; the other bond questions are decided separately.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Lets Rogers borrow up to $32.75 million for fire-department facilities and equipment, with related site and utility improvements. The bonds depend on approval of the separate refunding-bonds question. A replacement 1% city sales and use tax would repay approved bonds; it replaces the existing bond tax beginning the day after that tax expires, stays at 1% even if several bond questions pass, and ends when the bonds are paid or payment is otherwise legally provided for.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize up to $32.75 million in bonds for these improvements, subject to approval of the refunding question and repayment through the replacement 1% tax.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this bond authorization for this purpose; the other bond questions are decided separately.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Lets Rogers borrow up to $20.75 million for police-department facilities and equipment, with related site and utility improvements. The bonds depend on approval of the separate refunding-bonds question. A replacement 1% city sales and use tax would repay approved bonds; it replaces the existing bond tax beginning the day after that tax expires, stays at 1% even if several bond questions pass, and ends when the bonds are paid or payment is otherwise legally provided for.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize up to $20.75 million in bonds for these improvements, subject to approval of the refunding question and repayment through the replacement 1% tax.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this bond authorization for this purpose; the other bond questions are decided separately.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Lets Rogers borrow up to $8.75 million for animal-services buildings and equipment, with related site and utility improvements. The bonds depend on approval of the separate refunding-bonds question. A replacement 1% city sales and use tax would repay approved bonds; it replaces the existing bond tax beginning the day after that tax expires, stays at 1% even if several bond questions pass, and ends when the bonds are paid or payment is otherwise legally provided for.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize up to $8.75 million in bonds for these improvements, subject to approval of the refunding question and repayment through the replacement 1% tax.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this bond authorization for this purpose; the other bond questions are decided separately.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Lets Siloam Springs borrow up to $55 million for wastewater-treatment and sewer-system improvements. A 0.625% city sales and use tax would repay the bonds, replacing the existing 2018 water-bond tax of the same rate beginning the day after it expires. The new tax ends once the bonds are paid or payment is otherwise legally provided for, and bond proceeds may also cover a repayment reserve and issuance costs.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the wastewater bonds and their replacement 0.625% sales and use tax.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this wastewater-bond and replacement-tax proposal.
